title: Post perf-canary regression alerts to #eng-oncall with structured context + runbook links
author: Rafael Mendes
description:
## Summary
This PR wires perf-canary regression alerts into incident-bot so we post a single, structured message to `#eng-oncall` with the key context needed for first-pass triage.

Goals:
- Make the alert actionable without clicking through multiple systems.
- Standardize fields so responders can quickly compare slices (model/region/GPU/runtime build/scheduler mode).
- Include canonical runbook + dashboard links.
- Keep noise low: dedup grouping + guardrails around missing fields.

Non-goals:
- Not implementing the regression detector itself (owned by perf-canary + slo-toolkit).
- Not adding new Slack channels or changing PagerDuty routing here.

## What changes
### 1) New alert type: `perf_canary.regression`
- Accepts a payload from perf-canary webhook (see sample payload below).
- Emits a Block Kit message with consistent sections:
  - Header: severity + affected slice
  - Metrics: current vs baseline (p95 latency + tokens/sec), % deltas
  - Attribution: runtime_build + git_sha, scheduler_mode, kernel_id (when present)
  - Fleet: region + gpu_sku, request class
  - Links: Grafana dashboard deep link, detector details, runbook
  - Footer: dedup key + event time + suppression flags

### 2) Dedup + grouping
- Dedup key format (stable ordering):
  `perf-canary|<model>|<region>|<gpu_sku>|<runtime_build>|<metric>`
- Ensures we don’t spam `#eng-oncall` on every evaluation tick.
- Adds a soft rate-limit (per dedup key) to 1 post / 15 minutes; subsequent events update the thread (reply) with deltas if we can find the original message.

### 3) Runbook + dashboard links
- Runbook link points at: `runbook-perf-canary-regression-triage` (Confluence).
- Dashboard link is computed from labels (model/region/gpu_sku) into the perf-canary Grafana dashboard with pre-filled variables.

### 4) Safety / validation
- Rejects payloads missing required fields (model, region, regression_metric, current_value, baseline_value, severity). If missing, we still post a minimal message but label it `INCOMPLETE_PAYLOAD` and include the raw event id.
- Sanitizes strings to avoid Slack rendering injection and truncates long fields (kernel_fallback_reason, etc.).

## Sample message layout
- Title: `P1 Perf regression: llama-3.1-70b-instruct / us-east / H100`
- Fields:
  - `p95_latency_ms`: `412 -> 535 (+29.9%)`
  - `tokens_per_sec`: `128 -> 101 (-21.1%)`
  - `baseline`: `rolling_median_7d`
  - `runtime_build`: `runtime-2026.01.31.2 (git 8f3c2b1)`
  - `scheduler_mode`: `pinned_v2_no_heuristic_x`
  - `kernel_id`: `fa2_v3_128x128`
  - `request_class`: `canary-safe`
- Links:
  - `Grafana: Perf Canary / Model View`
  - `Runbook: Perf Canary Regression Triage`

## Notes
- This intentionally posts to `#eng-oncall` (not the incident channel) for visibility during phase-1 rollout.
- The channel name is configured via `PERF_CANARY_SLACK_CHANNEL` env var with a default of `#eng-oncall` in prod.

## Testing
- Unit tests cover:
  - Block formatting + truncation
  - Dedup key stability
  - Rate limit behavior
  - Missing field behavior
- Manual test performed against the staging Slack workspace using a replayed event (sanitized).

## Rollout plan
- Deploy incident-bot with this PR behind feature flag `PERF_CANARY_SLACK_ENABLED`.
- Enable in staging first; then prod with `severity >= P1` only for the first 48 hours.

## Related
- Linear: ENG-2853 (incident-bot annotations)
- Links referenced by payload:
  - Grafana perf-canary dashboards (observability-pack)
  - Runbook (SRE)

---

### Payload contract (from perf-canary)
Required:
- `severity`: P0|P1|P2
- `model`
- `region`
- `gpu_sku`
- `regression_metric`: `p95_latency_ms` | `tokens_per_sec`
- `current_value`, `baseline_value`, `delta_pct`
- `baseline_strategy`
Recommended:
- `runtime_build`, `runtime_git_sha`, `scheduler_mode`, `kernel_id`, `kernel_fallback_reason`
- `dashboard_url`, `runbook_url`, `detector_url`

incident-bot treats unknown fields as passthrough and includes them in a collapsed `raw` section for debugging.

review_conversation: Tomáš Novák: Can we make the runbook link canonical and not rely on the payload always including it? Also suggest adding a short 'what to do first' bullet list in the Slack message.

Rafael Mendes (author): Yep. I switched to using our Confluence shortlink as the default and only use payload runbook_url if present + allowlisted. For the Slack message, I added a compact 'Triage:' line with: check deploy annotation, compare GPU/region slices, follow runbook.
Sean Gallagher: Dedup key should include metric type; otherwise latency + tps regressions will collapse. Also please rate limit posts; #eng-oncall gets noisy fast.

Rafael Mendes (author): Updated dedup key to include `regression_metric` and added a 15m per-key rate limit. When we’re rate limited we reply in-thread (if we have the message ts) rather than dropping the signal.

Allison Grant: Please ensure we don’t expand label cardinality here by including raw tags in the message. Keep it to the approved fields (model, region, gpu_sku, runtime_build, scheduler_mode). Kernel ID is fine but truncate fallback reason.
Rafael Mendes (author): Done. Kernel fallback reason is truncated to 140 chars; extra fields go into a collapsed 'raw' section with strict length caps.
Felix Schneider: Dashboard link should land on the per-model view with variables pre-filled. I added the variable names in a comment on the PR (var-model, var-region, var-gpu).
Rafael Mendes (author): Pulled the variable mapping into config and added a unit test that URL-encodes the variables correctly.
Tomáš Novák: Approved after runbook/link changes. ✅
Sean Gallagher: Approved with rate limiting + metric in dedup key. ✅
